newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Chile firms are winners in Colombia power sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Chile firms are winners in Colombia power sell-off.

text.p: Chilean companies have emerged as the big winners in the first phase of Colombia's power plant privatization program.

The Energy Trade and Finance Corporation, a subsidiary of Chile's Chilgener, bought the 1,000 megawatt (MW) Chivor hydro- electric plant, in central Colombia, Friday after submitting a winning bid of 644.5 billion pesos.

The day before, the Endesa-Colombia consortium, composed of Chile's Endesa and 25 percent Colombian finance company Corfivalle, snapped up a 99 percent of the 499 MW Betania hydro- electric generator, in the southwest, for 302 billion pesos.

"We're proud to announce that two Chilean companies have teamed up with Colombia to provide electricity generating services," Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo said at an event to reveal the results of the Chivor bidding process.
The government, through its Mines and Energy Ministry, put seven power plants on the auction block in the first phase of its energy sector privatization.

Termocartagena, on the Caribbean coast was also sold Thursday and the winning bids for Ocoa, Gualanday and Yumbo, will be unveiled later Friday. Venezuela's Electricidad de Caracas purchased 14.25 percent of Termocartagena for 2.6 billion pesos.
The sell-off of the 150 megawatt Termatasajero, in central Colombia, was scrapped after the Mines and Energy Ministry ruled that no suitable bid had been submitted.
Nine foreign companies, from Chile, Venezuela, Germany, Spain and Britain, submitted valid bids for the process.

Endesa general manager Jaime Bauza told Reuters he was working on a plan to restructure Betania's debt which stands at about $200 million. Investment bank J.P. Morgan is helping to restructure tha plant's financial plan, which Bauza said would probably consist of extended debt repayment periods and negotiating more favorable interest rates.
"The (Betania) power plant is in good shape. It's been well- managed and the rules of the game in Colombia's energy sector are very stable which is why we entered the market," Bauza said.
He explained the 302 billion peso purchase price for Betania had been covered with Endesa's own funds and with some foreign credit, which he did not specify.
Chilgener executives declined to comment after the purchase of Chivor.
